Type: Neuralware
Install: Mall
Humanity Loss: None
Option Slots: uses 0

Iconic Chipware. It can write a personality into a dead host, provided the organs could still sustain life and the brain isn't gone. In a compatible corpse's shard slot, the body wakes inside the hour as the implanted personality, remembering only what predates the copy: same STATs, cyberware and afflictions as the body's previous owner, but free to move Skills and Role to equivalent Levels or Ranks elsewhere, and to trade LUCK against INT or COOL, or against any non-BODY stat. In a living host it works differently. Once in, it cannot come out without killing them, and at first it does nothing. The next time the user is Mortally Wounded and either fails a Death Save or goes unconscious after being stabilized, they don't die: 6 hours later they wake at 5 HP, Seriously Wounded. From then the chip projects its engram into their sight, the two sets of memories and mannerisms blending, and the user can talk to it and draw on what it knows. In that state their EMP becomes Stability (STAB), set to 10, while Empathy-based checks use the maximum EMP they started play with - and no source of Humanity Loss touches them, cyberpsychosis included. Every week costs 2d6 STAB, or 4d6 a week once STAB drops below 5. Stability never comes back, though a GM may cut a week's loss by 1d6 for time spent on things that don't tax the mind - loved ones, meditation, rest. Each threshold it crosses brings its own effect, from extra STAT points at 10 down to losing 5 maximum HP an hour and gaining Death Save penalties at 0.

Foundry notes:

  • Iconic: it can't be bought or sourced on the street, can't be fabricated without its Blueprint, can't be taken during Character Generation, and once acquired can't be destroyed unless the player agrees to it beforehand.
  • Corgo's Stability Chart lays out what happens at each STAB threshold; the full chart is in the document and in this item's text under the original-wording build. Stability is not a CPR stat, so nothing here is automated: track STAB by hand, on the EMP line or on a note.
  • Cannot be fabricated or Tech Upgraded, so it has no price; it has to be gifted or stolen.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Becoming Iconic > Iconic Cyberware).
